title: GET /api/status/<id> starts indexing as a side effect
description:
Onboarding: read AGENTS.md first (test command, push-to-main deploys prod, sandbox limits, bd workflow). Source: 2026-09-29 review of https://arxivbot.org; ticket cold-read QA'd 2026-09-30.

PROBLEM
GET /api/status/<id> (get_status, src/arxivbot/routes/api.py:199-227) starts a background index job when status is not_started, and again when an errored paper is past its 60s cooldown (should_retry_after_error, paper_service.py:421; ERROR_RETRY_COOLDOWN at line 73). Observed in prod 2026-09-29: first GET for 9999.99999 returned 'starting'. Any crawler, link-preview bot or prefetcher issuing a GET can trigger arXiv downloads on the 512MB VM. The chat page depends on this: checkStatus() (templates/chat.html:257) polls GET to kick off indexing.

CHANGE
1. get_status becomes read-only: return the current status, never schedule work. Remove its BackgroundTasks parameter.
2. POST /api/index/<id> (api.py:230) becomes the only trigger:
   - Add `request: Request` as the first parameter and `@limiter.limit("10/minute")` (slowapi needs the request parameter; see the chat endpoints at api.py:70-72).
   - Accept query parameter `auto` (bool, default false). Without auto: behaviour unchanged (starts on not_started or on any error; this is the manual Retry button, chat.html retryIndexing). With auto=1: start on not_started; on error start only if should_retry_after_error(status) is true; otherwise do nothing and report the current state.
3. templates/chat.html: on page load, call POST /api/index/${paperId}?auto=1 once, then start the existing checkStatus() polling. Ignore a failed POST (polling still runs).
Indexing on first chat message already works without any of this (query_paper calls fetch_paper_content directly); do not change it.

TESTS TO REWRITE (they assert the old GET behaviour)
- tests/test_arxiv_fetch.py:127-166: test_status_error_after_cooldown_retriggers_indexing and test_status_error_within_cooldown_does_not_retrigger -> move to POST /api/index?auto=1.
- tests/test_arxiv_id.py around lines 121 and 127 hit GET status; they will now see not_started.
acceptance_criteria:
- Test: GET /api/status/<new id> returns not_started and index_paper is not scheduled (mock and assert not called); calling it twice still returns not_started.
- Tests: POST /api/index/<id>?auto=1 starts on not_started; on error within cooldown does not start; on error after cooldown starts. POST without auto starts on error regardless of cooldown.
- Test: POST /api/index is rate limited (follow tests/test_rate_limit.py).
- Test: GET /abs/<id> HTML contains a fetch of '/api/index/' with 'auto=1'.
- uv run pytest -q passes.
- After deploy, using an ID unlikely to be indexed (pick a real recent paper, not one named in these tickets): two GETs of https://arxivbot.org/api/status/<id> five seconds apart both return not_started.
- Not verified by this ticket (say so in close reason): the progress banner in a real browser. Covered by the visual review ticket kca.
close_reason: Done: GET /api/status is read-only; POST /api/index is the only trigger, rate limited 10/minute, with auto=1 honouring the error cooldown; chat.html POSTs ?auto=1 once on load then polls. Validation: 119 tests pass; after deploy two GETs of /api/status/2509.04321 five seconds apart both returned not_started. NOT verified: progress banner in a real browser (deferred to kca). Guess: auto=1 within cooldown returns {'message': 'Retry cooldown active'}. Follow-up filed for the stuck-banner case when the page-load POST fails.

title: Nonexistent arXiv IDs render a normal chat page with HTTP 200
description:
Onboarding: read AGENTS.md first (test command, push-to-main deploys prod, sandbox limits, bd workflow). Source: 2026-09-29 review of https://arxivbot.org; ticket cold-read QA'd 2026-09-30.

PROBLEM
GET /abs/9999.99999 returns 200 with the full chat UI and the raw ID as the title. The failure only appears later via /api/status ('No source available'). A mistyped ID looks like a real paper.

CAUSES (verified)
a) new_chat_page (src/arxivbot/routes/pages.py:17-54) treats 'no metadata' as 'no title' and renders anyway.
b) fetch_paper_metadata (paper_service.py:635) returns None for four different cases: invalid ID, non-200 from arXiv, 200 with no <entry>, and any exception. For a missing paper the arXiv API returns HTTP 200 with totalResults 0 and no <entry> (same for a nonexistent version such as 1706.03762v99). Only that case means not-found.
c) Paper metadata is never stored: fetch_paper_content upserts Paper(title=None, authors=None, abstract=None) (paper_service.py:507-514) and db.upsert_paper (db.py:133) overwrites title/abstract on conflict. So every /abs view calls the arXiv API.

CHANGE
1. Make fetch_paper_metadata distinguish not-found from failure: raise a new PaperNotFound exception for '200 and no entry'; keep returning None for transient failures. Update callers in pages.py (both /abs and /chat).
2. Persist metadata: when /abs fetches metadata successfully, upsert title/abstract/authors. Change upsert_paper's ON CONFLICT to COALESCE(excluded.x, papers.x) for title, authors, abstract so the indexing upsert no longer nulls them.
3. On PaperNotFound, /abs returns 404 rendering new templates/error.html: brand header linking to /, heading 'No arXiv paper with ID <id>', a link to https://arxiv.org/search/, and the paper form. Do not render the chat UI, so no indexing starts.
4. Extract the home page form into templates/_paper_form.html and its script (home.html:68-91) into static/paper-form.js; home.html and error.html both include them. error.html takes (status_code, heading, message) so ticket bi9 can reuse it.
A transient arXiv failure must still render the chat page with the ID as title (never 404 a real paper because export.arxiv.org is slow). No negative caching is required.
acceptance_criteria:
- Test: fetch_paper_metadata raises PaperNotFound for an Atom feed with no <entry> (mock _arxiv_get), returns None when _arxiv_get returns a non-200 or raises.
- Test: /abs/<id> returns 404 HTML containing the ID and the paper form when metadata lookup raises PaperNotFound.
- Test: /abs/<id> returns 200 chat page with the ID as title when metadata lookup returns None.
- Test: after one successful /abs/<id> view, a second view does not call fetch_paper_metadata (assert call count), and the title survives a subsequent upsert_paper with title=None.
- Test: / still renders the form (now via the partial).
- uv run pytest -q passes.
- After deploy: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://arxivbot.org/abs/9999.99999 prints 404; https://arxivbot.org/abs/1706.03762 prints 200.
close_reason: Done: fetch_paper_metadata raises PaperNotFound on 200-with-no-entry, /abs returns 404 via new templates/error.html (+ _paper_form.html partial, static/paper-form.js), metadata persisted on /abs view, upsert_paper COALESCEs title/authors/abstract. Validation: 110 tests pass; after deploy /abs/9999.99999 -> 404, /abs/1706.03762 -> 200. Guesses: /chat/<slug> on PaperNotFound still renders the saved chat; error.html copy ('Check the ID for typos...', 'Try another paper') was not specified; arXiv search link shows on every error page (bi9 may want a flag).

title: Add link-preview metadata (Open Graph, Twitter card, description, canonical) and a favicon
description:
Onboarding: read AGENTS.md first (test command, push-to-main deploys prod, sandbox limits, bd workflow). Source: 2026-09-29 review of https://arxivbot.org; ticket cold-read QA'd 2026-09-30.

PROBLEM
Neither template has a meta description, Open Graph tags, Twitter card tags or a canonical link, and /favicon.ico is 404. A pasted arxivbot.org link unfurls as a bare URL in Slack, X, iMessage, Discord.

DEPENDS ON dgd, which persists paper title/abstract/authors and adds templates/error.html. Build on that.

CHANGE
1. src/arxivbot/config.py: add SITE_URL (env var, default 'https://arxivbot.org'). Build all absolute URLs from it; do not use request.base_url (uvicorn runs without --proxy-headers, so it yields http://).
2. New partial templates/_meta.html, included in the <head> of home.html, chat.html and error.html. It renders: <meta name="description">, <link rel="canonical">, og:title, og:description, og:url, og:type=website, og:site_name=ArxivBot, og:image, twitter:card=summary, <link rel="icon" href="/static/favicon.svg" type="image/svg+xml">. Error pages get no canonical.
3. Values:
   - / : title 'ArxivBot - Chat with arXiv Papers'; description 'Add "bot" after "arxiv" in any arXiv paper URL to ask questions about the paper and get answers quoted from its text.'; canonical SITE_URL + '/'.
   - /abs/<id>: og:title = paper title (fallback: 'arXiv <id>'); description = abstract with whitespace collapsed, truncated to 200 chars plus '...' (fallback: 'Ask questions about arXiv paper <id> and get answers quoted from its text.'); canonical SITE_URL + '/abs/<canonical id>'.
   - /chat/<slug>: og:title = 'Chat about: <paper title or arXiv id>'; description = 'A conversation about this paper on ArxivBot.'; canonical = the chat URL. Do NOT put the user's question or any message text in metadata (privacy decision).
4. pages.py: pass abstract through to the template for /abs and /chat (from the db row, else fetch_paper_metadata).
5. Assets, committed under static/: favicon.svg (letter 'A', white on rgb(140,21,21), square); favicon.ico (32x32); og.png (512x512, same mark). Generate the raster files with a one-off script, e.g. `uv run --with pillow python ...`; do not add pillow to project dependencies. Add a GET /favicon.ico route returning static/favicon.ico.
All values rely on Jinja autoescaping; titles and abstracts contain quotes, $ and LaTeX.
acceptance_criteria:
- TestClient tests (metadata monkeypatched): /abs/<id> response contains og:title, og:description, og:url, og:image, og:site_name, twitter:card, a meta description and a canonical link with the https://arxivbot.org/abs/<id> URL.
- Test: a title containing a double quote and '<' renders escaped (no raw quote inside the content attribute).
- Test: with metadata unavailable, /abs/<id> renders the fallback title and description; no content="" attributes.
- Test: a seeded chat page contains og:title starting 'Chat about:' and does not contain the seeded user message text inside <head>.
- Test: / contains the home description; /favicon.ico returns 200.
- uv run pytest -q passes.
- After deploy, each prints 1 or more: for p in og:title og:description og:url og:image twitter:card; do curl -s https://arxivbot.org/abs/1706.03762 | grep -c "$p"; done. Also curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' for /favicon.ico and /static/og.png returns 200.
- Owner step, not part of acceptance: paste a link into Slack or opengraph.xyz to eyeball the preview.
close_reason: Done: templates/_meta.html (description, canonical, og:title/description/url/type/site_name/image, twitter:card, icon) included in home, chat and error heads; values per ticket; /favicon.ico route; static/favicon.svg, favicon.ico, og.png committed. Validation: 164 tests pass; after deploy each of og:title, og:description, og:url, og:image, twitter:card greps 1 on /abs/1706.03762; /favicon.ico and /static/og.png return 200. Owner step not done: eyeball a real preview in Slack/X. Notes: chat canonical/og:url contain the slug, which is derived from the first question (ticket said canonical = chat URL); error pages use heading/message as og:title/description; abstract cut at exactly 200 chars; /abs canonical uses the ID as requested in the URL.

title: Chat landing: say what the page is and offer suggested starter questions
description:
Onboarding: read AGENTS.md first (test command, push-to-main deploys prod, sandbox limits, bd workflow). Source: 2026-09-29 review of https://arxivbot.org; ticket cold-read QA'd 2026-09-30.

PROBLEM
Most visitors arrive by adding 'bot' to an arxiv.org URL, so /abs/<id> is the real landing page. Its empty state is one line (templates/chat.html:80-82, .welcome-message): 'Ask a question about this paper to start the conversation.' Nothing says what ArxivBot is and there is nothing to click.

CHANGE (templates/chat.html, static/style.css)
Replace the contents of .welcome-message with exactly:
- Paragraph: 'ArxivBot answers questions about this paper and quotes the passages it relies on.'
- Four <button type="button" class="starter"> elements, in this order: 'Summarize this paper' / 'What is the main contribution?' / 'What are the limitations?' / 'Explain the method step by step'
Clicking a starter calls the existing send path with the button text as the message (doSendMessage(text, true) at chat.html:344, which already removes .welcome-message at line 355). If sendBtn is disabled (a request is in flight) the click does nothing. If the send fails the starters do not come back; the existing error + Retry bubble covers that. The block is rendered only when the page has no messages (same condition as today), so /chat/<slug> pages with history never show it.
Style: wrap buttons in a flex row that wraps; usable at 375px wide without horizontal scroll.

OUT OF SCOPE: per-paper generated questions (would spend LLM quota per page view).

Note: v2i changes the page-load JS in the same file and must land first (dependency set).

- TestClient test: GET /abs/1706.03762 (with fetch_paper_metadata monkeypatched as in tests/test_pages.py) contains the orientation sentence and exactly four button.starter elements with the four strings above.
- TestClient test: a chat seeded with one turn (see chat_service.save_turn and tests/test_chat_persistence.py) rendered at /chat/<slug> contains no 'class="starter"'.
- uv run pytest -q passes.
- After deploy: `curl -s https://arxivbot.org/abs/2603.14732v1 | grep -c 'class="starter"'` prints 4, and the same grep on https://arxivbot.org/chat/what-is-the-main-finding-in-two-sentences-fd13972a prints 0.

Validation: 140 tests pass; after deploy grep -c 'class="starter"' prints 4 on /abs/2603.14732v1 and 0 on the fixture chat. title: Use Fly suspend instead of stop so scale-to-zero wakes in under a second
description:
Onboarding: read AGENTS.md first (test command, push-to-main deploys prod, sandbox limits, bd workflow). Source: 2026-09-29 review of https://arxivbot.org; ticket cold-read QA'd 2026-09-30.

PROBLEM
A request to / after the machine had been idle took 7.2s; warm requests take ~0.25s. fly.toml has auto_stop_machines = 'stop' and min_machines_running = 0, so visitors arriving via a spliced arxiv URL often wait on a blank tab while the container and Python cold boot. The owner will not pay for an always-on machine: do not set min_machines_running = 1 and do not add an uptime pinger.

CHANGE
In fly.toml set auto_stop_machines = 'suspend'. Nothing else. Fly then snapshots VM memory and resumes it instead of cold booting; suspended machines are billed like stopped ones. The VM (512MB, no swap) meets Fly's suspend requirements. Do not touch DATABASE_PATH or the arxivbot_data mount.

HOW TO MEASURE (no fly CLI needed)
An idle machine is stopped/suspended by Fly after several minutes without requests. 'Idle sample' = make no requests to arxivbot.org or arxivbot.fly.dev for 15 minutes, then run: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{time_starttransfer}\n' https://arxivbot.org/health
Take 3 idle samples BEFORE the change (baseline) and 3 AFTER the deploy finishes. The first request after a deploy does not count.

STATE THAT SURVIVES A RESUME (check these, not connections)
aiohttp sessions and aiosqlite connections are opened per call, so there are no stale handles. Long-lived in-process state is: the litellm _router singleton, the slowapi in-memory limiter, _content_cache, and _indexing_status with its time.time() error cooldown (paper_service.py). After resume these persist instead of resetting; that is acceptable, just confirm nothing errors.

OWNER-ONLY (not part of acceptance): `fly machines list` showing state 'suspended', and the Fly invoice. Mention in the close reason that these were not checked.
acceptance_criteria:
- fly.toml has auto_stop_machines = 'suspend'; no other config change.
- uv run pytest -q passes; pushed to main; the 'Fly Deploy' GitHub Actions run succeeded (gh run list).
- Close reason records 3 baseline and 3 post-change idle samples. Pass if the post-change median is under 1.5s. If it is not, revert the change, record the numbers, and close as 'suspend did not help'.
- Immediately after one post-change idle sample, all return 200 with read-only GETs: /, /abs/2603.14732v1, /api/status/2603.14732v1, and https://arxivbot.org/chat/what-is-the-main-finding-in-two-sentences-fd13972a
- No POST to the production chat API.
close_reason: Done: fly.toml auto_stop_machines='suspend' (commit 3bfa8b6), Fly Deploy run succeeded. Idle samples of /health time_starttransfer: baseline 6.83s, 7.72s, 7.21s (median 7.21s; third taken after ~35 min idle); post-change 0.92s, 0.33s, 0.27s (median 0.33s; third taken after ~57 min idle) - passes <1.5s. After the third post sample, GET /, /abs/2603.14732v1, /api/status/2603.14732v1 and the fixture chat all returned 200. No POSTs to prod. NOT checked (owner-only): 'fly machines list' showing state suspended, and the Fly invoice.

Pro models have 0 quota; Gemma 4 has 16K TPM, too small for a paper. Make gemini-3.8-flash primary and fall back on errors through 3.7/3.6/3.5/3-flash-preview (20 RPD each), then 3.5-flash-lite and 3.1-flash-lite (15 RPM, 500 RPD each), then the paid key if configured. title: Docker build ignores uv.lock (pip install . pulls newest litellm/aiohttp/slowapi)
description: Pre-deploy review (2026-09-29). Dockerfile runs 'pip install --no-cache-dir .' against unpinned ranges in pyproject.toml, so every deploy gets the latest litellm, aiohttp and slowapi. The code depends on litellm Router details and aiohttp.http_exceptions.ContentLengthError. An upstream release can break a deploy. Fix: install from the lockfile (uv sync --frozen --no-dev) or pin upper bounds. Needs a real docker build to verify, which the sandbox can't do.
close_reason: Done: Dockerfile uses pinned uv 0.10.12 + uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-editable; dropped build-essential (all runtime deps have cp311 wheels). Verified: CI deploy build log installs fastapi==0.128.0 starlette==0.50.0 (lock versions); prod /health, /, /abs 200 after deploy.

title: Rate limiter keys on the Fly proxy IP (all users share one bucket) and honors spoofable X_FORWARDED_FOR
description:
**Status: INFERRED from code; can't be verified in prod because the limiter isn't deployed yet.**

src/arxivbot/limiter.py keys on `slowapi.util.get_ipaddr`, which checks `request.headers["X_FORWARDED_FOR"]` (underscores, not the standard X-Forwarded-For) and otherwise uses `request.client.host`. The Dockerfile runs `uvicorn ... --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000` without `--proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips='*'`. Behind Fly's proxy, `request.client.host` is the Fly proxy address, so:
- All users probably share one 5/minute bucket (one busy user locks everyone out), and
- A client that sends an `X_FORWARDED_FOR: <random>` header gets a fresh bucket each request, bypassing the limit (if Fly passes underscore headers through, which is unverified).

Expected: key on the real client IP. Use Fly's `Fly-Client-IP` header, or run uvicorn with `--proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips='*'` and use `get_remote_address`.
Verify after deploy: two different client IPs should get independent limits, and sending `X_FORWARDED_FOR` shouldn't reset the count.
Severity: high. It blocks deploying main.
close_reason: Done: limiter keys on Fly-Client-IP (fallback client.host), ignores X-Forwarded-For/X_FORWARDED_FOR. Validation: pytest 10 passed incl. TestClient 429 on 6th request per Fly-Client-IP; tests fail on old code. Live verification pending deploy (9ex).

title: Transient arXiv fetch errors (406, ContentLengthError) are not retried and stick as permanent paper errors
description:
**Status: VERIFIED (2026-09-29).** Transient arXiv fetch failures become sticky "error" states with no retry.

Repro (probe of 18 IDs fired in a burst via `GET /api/status/{id}`):
- `0704.0001v1` → `{"status":"error","error":"Failed to fetch source: HTTP 406"}`, while `0704.0001` (same paper, no version) → complete.
- `1706.03762v99` (nonexistent version) → `HTTP 406` on the first try, then `No source available` (the correct 404) on retry.
- `2401.00001v1` → `Response payload is not completed: <ContentLengthError: 400, message='Not enough data to satisfy content length header.'>`
- `2603.14732v1` (the 406 in the earlier session) → complete now.
After `curl -X POST https://arxivbot.org/api/index/<id>` (which re-runs on the error state), 0704.0001v1 and 2401.00001v1 both became `complete` on the first retry. From the sandbox, arxiv.org/src returns 200 for all of these.

Conclusion: the 406s and truncated bodies from arXiv are intermittent. They're likely burst or bot throttling of Fly egress (inferred), not a permanent IP block. The app turns them into permanent failures:
1. `fetch_paper_content` (src/arxivbot/services/paper_service.py ~L149-156) does one bare aiohttp GET with no retry/backoff, no timeout, and no User-Agent/Accept headers. It treats every non-200 other than 404 as fatal.
2. `GET /api/status` (src/arxivbot/routes/api.py ~L203-208) only starts indexing on `not_started`. `_indexing_status[paper_id] = {"status":"error"}` stays in memory until the process restarts, so reloading the page never retries.
3. The UI (templates/chat.html ~L257) shows `Error: Failed to fetch source: HTTP 406` with no retry control. Sending a chat message does re-fetch, but the banner keeps showing the stale error.

Expected: retry transient errors (406/429/5xx/ContentLengthError/timeouts) with backoff and a descriptive User-Agent (arXiv asks for one). Consider export.arxiv.org as a fallback. Let /api/status re-trigger indexing on `error` (with a cooldown), or expire error entries. Show a user-facing message with a Retry button, and don't show raw aiohttp exception text.
The same bare-session pattern applies to `fetch_paper_metadata` (~L311) and `fetch_ar5iv_html` (~L363).
Severity: high. Random papers are unusable for the lifetime of the machine.
close_reason: Done: shared _arxiv_get helper (UA, timeouts, retries 406/429/5xx/payload/timeout at 2/5/15s, Retry-After, 404 fatal, 2-slot semaphore); friendly errors; /api/status re-triggers after 60s error cooldown; Retry button in chat.html. Metadata/html retry once to avoid stalling page render. Validation: pytest 19 passed (aioresponses mocks). Live check pending deploy.

title: Prod is running stale code (~10839b7): /html route, rate limiting, Gemini retry/fallback, Enter fix not deployed
description:
**Status: VERIFIED (2026-09-29).** Production (https://arxivbot.org) is running code from about commit 10839b7 (2026-02-08). None of the commits from 2026-02-12 onward are live.

Evidence:
- `curl -s https://arxivbot.org/html/1706.03762` returns `{"detail":"Not Found"}` [404]. The /html route was added in 0913622 (issue arxivbot.org-6dn, closed).
- Rate limiting (7adaedc, arxivbot.org-x8i, closed) is not live: 9 back-to-back `POST /api/chat/stream` requests with `{"paper_id":"bogus","message":"x"}` all return 400, with no 429. The limiter runs before the handler body, so a 429 was expected from the 6th request on.
- The served chat.html still has `document.getElementById('chat-form').dispatchEvent(new Event('submit'))`, which is the pre-deb48b7 Enter handler. A diff of the served /abs page against `git show <c>:templates/chat.html` is smallest for 10839b7 (32 lines) and largest for HEAD (102 lines).
- So the Gemini retry (6abb89e, arxivbot.org-ubr) and the paid fallback Router (acb3f81, arxivbot.org-aqa) are almost certainly not live either (inferred).

Expected: prod matches main (or the closed issues get reopened).
Fix: `just deploy`, but only after arxivbot.org rate-limiter keying is fixed (see the blocking dependency). Otherwise the first deploy makes all users share one 5/min bucket.
Also check why the deploy didn't happen: cbde8f8 added a GitHub Actions deploy. Is it failing or disabled?
notes: Root cause (verified 2026-09-29): local main is 10 commits ahead of origin/main (0b4b8cf); nothing since Feb 8 was pushed. .github/workflows/fly-deploy.yml deploys on push to main, so pushing = deploying. The workflow isn't on origin yet; FLY_API_TOKEN secret existence unknown.
close_reason: Done: pushed main (root cause: never pushed; GH Actions fly-deploy now runs on push). Deploy b8833a7 broke all HTML pages (Starlette 1.7 via unpinned Docker deps, see fds); hotfix 811213b deployed ~10 min later. Verified on prod: /health ok without path; / and /abs 200; /html 302; math.AG/0211159 301->math/0211159 200; 429 on 6th bad-ID chat despite spoofed X-Forwarded-For; /ar5iv HEAD 200, 404 page has marker; empty msg 422; Retry button served.

title: Add slowapi rate limiting to chat API endpoints
description:
## Goal

Protect Gemini free tier quota (10 RPM, 250 RPD) from abuse by rate-limiting the chat API endpoints per IP.

## Implementation

### 1. Add dependency
Add slowapi to pyproject.toml dependencies.

### 2. Create limiter module
New file: src/arxivbot/limiter.py

Use get_ipaddr (not get_remote_address) as key_func — Fly.io puts a proxy in front of the app, so we need X-Forwarded-For. In-memory storage is fine for single-instance Fly.io (no Redis needed). Counters reset on deploy which is acceptable.

### 3. Wire into main.py (src/arxivbot/main.py)
- Import limiter, attach to app.state.limiter
- Add SlowAPIMiddleware
- Add ProxyHeadersMiddleware (from uvicorn) with trusted_hosts=['*'] for correct client IP behind Fly.io proxy
- Register custom 429 error handler that returns JSON (not plain text) so the frontend can handle it

### 4. Decorate chat endpoints (src/arxivbot/routes/api.py)
- @limiter.limit('5/minute') on /api/chat (line ~84) and /api/chat/stream (line ~109)
- IMPORTANT: endpoints need a request: Request param (from fastapi) separate from the Pydantic body model. Currently the body param may be named 'request' — rename it to 'chat_request' to avoid collision.
- Leave all other routes (health, status, pages) unlimited.

### 5. Frontend handling (templates/chat.html)
- Detect 429 responses and show a user-friendly 'Rate limited — please wait a moment' message instead of a generic error.
- Optionally show a countdown based on Retry-After header.

## Key gotchas
- Middleware order matters: ProxyHeadersMiddleware should be added AFTER SlowAPIMiddleware (so it executes first as outermost wrapper).
- slowapi requires request: Request in the function signature or it silently does nothing.
- SSE/streaming endpoints work fine — rate limit is checked at connection time, not per chunk.
- WebSockets are not supported by slowapi but we use SSE over HTTP so this is fine.

## Key files
- src/arxivbot/main.py — middleware setup
- src/arxivbot/routes/api.py:84-106 — /api/chat endpoint
- src/arxivbot/routes/api.py:109-177 — /api/chat/stream endpoint
- templates/chat.html:322-326 — non-streaming error display
- templates/chat.html:365-367 — streaming error display
- pyproject.toml — dependencies
close_reason: Implemented rate limiting for chat API endpoints using slowapi (5/minute per IP). Added custom 429 error handler returning JSON, frontend detection for rate limit errors.

title: Support /html/ URL paths (add bot before .org contract)
description:
## Problem

The arxivbot.org value prop is 'just change arxiv.org to arxivbot.org in any URL'. This works for /abs/ and /pdf/ paths, but NOT for /html/ paths. Visiting https://arxivbot.org/html/2510.04374v1 returns a 404 instead of loading the chat interface.

arXiv serves HTML-rendered papers at /html/ paths (e.g. https://arxiv.org/html/2510.04374v1), so users will naturally try the same substitution.

## Root Cause

1. **No /html/ route** — src/arxivbot/routes/pages.py has routes for /abs/ (line 15), /pdf/ (line 50), /ar5iv/ (line 111), but no /html/ route.

2. **URL parser ignores html/ prefix** — src/arxivbot/utils/arxiv.py:98 only strips 'abs/' and 'pdf/' prefixes, not 'html/':
   `for prefix in ('abs/', 'pdf/'):`

3. **Frontend regex DOES match /html/** — templates/home.html:77 already handles it in the URL input parser:
   `/(?:abs|pdf|html)\//`
   So the landing page URL bar works, but direct navigation does not.

## Key Files and Lines

- src/arxivbot/routes/pages.py:15 — /abs/ route (model for the fix)
- src/arxivbot/routes/pages.py:50-56 — /pdf/ route (redirects to /abs/, do the same for /html/)
- src/arxivbot/utils/arxiv.py:98 — prefix list needs 'html/' added
- templates/home.html:77 — frontend regex (already correct)

## Suggested Fix

1. Add a /html/ route in pages.py that redirects to /abs/{paper_id}, mirroring the /pdf/ route pattern (lines 50-56).
2. Add 'html/' to the prefix tuple in extract_arxiv_id_from_path() at arxiv.py:98.
3. Optionally update README.md to mention /html/ URL support.
close_reason: Added /html/ route in pages.py (redirects to /abs/) and added 'html/' to prefix list in extract_arxiv_id_from_path()

title: Add retry handling for Gemini API errors (503, rate limits)
description:
## Problem

When the Gemini backend returns a 503 (or similar transient error), the error propagates directly to the user as a generic 'Error: ...' message in the chat. There is no way to retry — the user must manually re-send their message.

## Root Cause

The LLM calls in paper_service.py have no retry logic. Errors bubble up through api.py as HTTP 500 / SSE error events, and the frontend just displays them inline with no retry affordance.

## Key Files and Lines

**Backend — LLM calls (no retry wrapping):**
- src/arxivbot/services/paper_service.py:208 — litellm.acompletion() in query_paper()
- src/arxivbot/services/paper_service.py:270 — litellm.acompletion() in query_paper_stream()

**Backend — error catch sites:**
- src/arxivbot/routes/api.py:104-106 — generic except Exception in /api/chat, raises HTTPException(500)
- src/arxivbot/routes/api.py:166-168 — generic except Exception in /api/chat/stream, sends SSE error

**Frontend — error display (no retry button):**
- templates/chat.html:325 — non-streaming error display: addMessage('assistant', 'Error: ...')
- templates/chat.html:365-366 — streaming error display: appends error text inline

## Suggested Fix

Two layers:

1. **Backend (silent retry):** Wrap litellm.acompletion() calls with retry logic for transient errors (503, 429, timeouts). litellm may have built-in retry support via num_retries param — check docs. Alternatively use tenacity.

2. **Frontend (retry UX):** When an error is displayed, show a 'Retry' button next to the error message that re-sends the last user message. This covers non-transient failures or exhausted retries.
close_reason: Added num_retries=3 to both litellm.acompletion() calls for automatic retry on transient errors (503, 429). Added frontend retry button on error messages so users can re-send without retyping.

title: Paper pane: HEAD /ar5iv returns 405, so unavailable HTML shows raw JSON in the iframe
description:
**Status: VERIFIED (2026-09-29, Chrome on prod).**

templates/chat.html ~L187 checks paper-pane availability with `fetch('/ar5iv/${paperId}', {method:'HEAD'})`. FastAPI GET routes don't answer HEAD:
`curl -sI https://arxivbot.org/ar5iv/1706.03762` → 405 (so do /abs, /pdf, and /chat/{slug}).

Effects:
- The HEAD check is always `!ok`, so it calls `showPaperError()` whenever it resolves before the iframe `load` event. When HTML exists, the pane can flash the error state until load fires (race).
- When HTML does not exist (`/ar5iv/9999.99999` → 404 JSON), the iframe still fires `load` (error pages fire load), and the load handler hides the error pane and shows the iframe. Result: the left pane displays raw `{"detail":"HTML view unavailable for paper 9999.99999. You can view the PDF at ..."}` in the browser's JSON viewer instead of the styled "paper-error" state. Seen live on https://arxivbot.org/abs/9999.99999.

Expected: the error pane (with a PDF link) shows when HTML is unavailable, and there's no flash when it is available.
Fix options: use GET for the probe (or `api_route(methods=["GET","HEAD"])`), and don't let the iframe `load` handler override a known failure. Alternatively, have /ar5iv return an HTML error page for the iframe instead of JSON.
Severity: medium (UX).
close_reason: Done: removed HEAD probe; /ar5iv returns HTML error pages (404 html-unavailable / 400 invalid-id) with arxivbot-error meta marker; iframe load handler inspects same-origin doc and shows styled error; /ar5iv answers HEAD. title: Add paid Gemini key as fallback via litellm Router
description:
## Goal

Use free tier Gemini 3 Flash as primary, with paid tier Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite as automatic fallback when rate-limited. This lets the app stay functional when free quota is exhausted.

## Prerequisites
- Create a second Google Cloud project with billing enabled
- Generate a paid-tier API key from that project
- Set as Fly.io secret: fly secrets set GEMINI_API_KEY_PAID=<key>

## Architecture

Free vs paid is PER-PROJECT in Google Cloud (not per-account). Two projects under one Google account:
- Project A (no billing): free tier key -> GEMINI_API_KEY (existing env var)
- Project B (billing enabled): paid tier key -> GEMINI_API_KEY_PAID (new env var)

litellm has native Router support for fallbacks between model deployments with different API keys.

## Implementation

### 1. Update config.py (src/arxivbot/config.py)
- Add GEMINI_API_KEY_PAID: str | None = None (optional, graceful if not set)
- Add config for fallback model name: llm_fallback_model = 'gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-lite'

### 2. Create litellm Router in paper_service.py (src/arxivbot/services/paper_service.py)
Replace direct litellm.acompletion() calls with a Router instance:

    from litellm import Router

    model_list = [
        {
            'model_name': 'gemini-primary',
            'litellm_params': {
                'model': 'gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview',
                'api_key': settings.gemini_api_key,
                'rpm': 10,
            }
        },
    ]
    # Only add fallback if paid key is configured
    if settings.gemini_api_key_paid:
        model_list.append({
            'model_name': 'gemini-fallback',
            'litellm_params': {
                'model': 'gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-lite',
                'api_key': settings.gemini_api_key_paid,
                'rpm': 300,
            }
        })

    router = Router(
        model_list=model_list,
        fallbacks=[{'gemini-primary': ['gemini-fallback']}] if settings.gemini_api_key_paid else [],
        num_retries=2,
        allowed_fails=1,
        cooldown_time=60,
    )

### 3. Replace acompletion calls
- paper_service.py:208 — change litellm.acompletion() to router.acompletion(model='gemini-primary', ...)
- paper_service.py:270 — same for streaming call

### 4. Graceful degradation
If GEMINI_API_KEY_PAID is not set, the Router should still work with just the primary model (no fallback). This keeps local dev simple — only need one key.

## Model details
- Primary: gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview (free, 10 RPM, 250 RPD)
- Fallback: gemini/gemini-2.5-flash-lite (paid, 300 RPM, 1500 RPD, $0.10/$0.40 per 1M tokens)

## Fallback behavior at runtime
1. Request -> gemini-primary (free)
2. On 429 -> retry 2x with exponential backoff
3. If still failing -> cooldown primary for 60s, fall back to gemini-fallback (paid)
4. After cooldown -> primary rejoins pool, next request tries free tier again

## Key files
- src/arxivbot/config.py:18-22 — API key and model config
- src/arxivbot/services/paper_service.py:208 — non-streaming LLM call

title: Brainstorm UX: LLM paper quotes with split-pane viewer and bidirectional highlighting
description:
Design UX for paper citation/quoting feature:

**Core concept:** When the LLM references or quotes from a paper, both the chat and paper viewer should be linked.

**Layout:**
- Chat on the left
- Paper viewer (PDF or rendered TeX) on the right in a split-pane

**Bidirectional linking:**
- Quotes in chat are clickable → scrolls/highlights the source in the paper viewer
- Passages in the paper viewer are highlightable → can link back to which chat messages referenced them

**Questions to explore:**
- How to identify quote boundaries in LLM output (special tokens, markdown syntax?)
- How to map quotes to paper locations (character offsets, section/paragraph IDs, page numbers?)
- Visual treatment of highlights (colors, animations, focus states)
- Mobile/responsive considerations for the split-pane
- What happens when multiple quotes reference nearby passages?
- Should quotes be stored for later reference or just session-based?

title: Run a visual and mobile review of the home and chat pages
description:
Onboarding: read AGENTS.md first. If you do not, leave it and say so; do not substitute a reading of the CSS. This ticket produces findings, not fixes.

WHY
The 2026-09-29 review covered accessibility rules, metadata, copy and URL handling. The automated screenshot reviewer produced no output (cause not diagnosed), so layout has never been looked at. Tickets 22s, 7gz and aua change the UI and explicitly defer their in-browser checks to this ticket; it is blocked on them so the findings describe the shipped UI.

PAGES (production, read-only)
A. https://arxivbot.org/
B. https://arxivbot.org/abs/2603.14732v1 (empty state with starter questions)
C. https://arxivbot.org/chat/what-is-the-main-finding-in-two-sentences-fd13972a (existing chat with an answer)

Each at 375x812, 768x1024 and 1280x800.

- Every concrete problem is filed as its own bd issue with `--deps discovered-from:arxivbot.org-kca`, with page, width, what is wrong, and the CSS/template location.

C /chat @375 PROBLEM 241px for messages (2vs); C @768 ok; C @1280 ok. D error page @375 ok; @768 ok; @1280 ok. No horizontal scroll anywhere except A@375. No console errors on any page. title: Redirect www.arxivbot.org to the apex domain
description:
Onboarding: read AGENTS.md first (test command, push-to-main deploys prod, sandbox limits, bd workflow). Source: 2026-09-29 review of https://arxivbot.org; ticket cold-read QA'd 2026-09-30.

PROBLEM (verified live)
https://www.arxivbot.org/abs/2603.14732v1 returns 200 with the same content as the apex domain, so every page exists at two URLs. People do arrive on www: www.arxiv.org URLs exist in the wild and splicing 'bot' into one lands on www.arxivbot.org.

CHANGE (src/arxivbot/main.py)
Add an HTTP middleware: if the request Host header (case-insensitive, port stripped) is exactly 'www.arxivbot.org', respond 308 with Location 'https://arxivbot.org' + path + ('?' + query if any). 308 preserves method and body, so POSTs to www keep working. All other hosts pass through untouched, including arxivbot.fly.dev (out of scope; Fly health checks and `just verify` use it) and the internal health probe.
Do not attempt a DNS- or Fly-level redirect (needs the owner's registrar account).
acceptance_criteria:
- Test: GET /abs/1706.03762?x=1 with header Host: www.arxivbot.org -> 308, Location == https://arxivbot.org/abs/1706.03762?x=1, and the route handler is not executed.
- Test: same request with Host: arxivbot.org and with Host: arxivbot.fly.dev is not redirected; /health returns 200 for any host other than www.
- uv run pytest -q passes.
- After deploy: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}' 'https://www.arxivbot.org/abs/1706.03762?x=1' prints '308 https://arxivbot.org/abs/1706.03762?x=1'; https://arxivbot.org/health and https://arxivbot.fly.dev/health return 200.
close_reason: Done: middleware in main.py 308-redirects Host www.arxivbot.org to https://arxivbot.org + path + query; other hosts untouched. Validation: 131 tests pass; after deploy 'https://www.arxivbot.org/abs/1706.03762?x=1' -> 308 https://arxivbot.org/abs/1706.03762?x=1; arxivbot.org/health and arxivbot.fly.dev/health -> 200.

title: Legacy arXiv IDs with a subject class (math.AG/0211159) rejected as invalid
description:
**Status: VERIFIED (2026-09-29).**

`curl -s -w '%{http_code}' https://arxivbot.org/abs/math.AG/0211159` → 400 `Invalid arXiv ID`. arXiv accepts old-style IDs with a subject class (`https://arxiv.org/abs/math.DG/0211159` 301-redirects to `/abs/math/0211159`). These forms appear in older citations, and users substituting arxiv.org → arxivbot.org will hit them.
Cause: `LEGACY_PATTERN = r"^([a-z-]+)/(\d{7})(v(\d+))?$"` in src/arxivbot/utils/arxiv.py L41 doesn't allow `.XX` subject classes.
Also: `/api/status/1706.03762V1` (uppercase V) → 400. That's minor.
Expected: accept `archive.SUBJ/YYMMNNN` and normalize it to `archive/YYMMNNN` (the version is keyed separately). Also consider normalizing so `1706.03762` and `1706.03762v7` don't cache/index separately.
Severity: low.
close_reason: Done: parser accepts archive.SUBJ/YYMMNNN and uppercase V, returns canonical id (math.AG/0211159 -> math/0211159); /abs 301s to canonical; routes/services key caches/status/DB on canonical id. Versioned vs unversioned kept distinct. Validation: pytest 73 passed (36 new).
